user_state: Inconsistent. Good days and bad days. Feels like always starting over. Progress feels invisible and the gaps feel larger than the returns.
core_need: Trust in the small daily return. To believe that coming back is the whole practice, not proof of failure.

arrival.heading: You came back.
arrival.subheading: That is the whole thing. Not perfection. Not the streak. The return.

arrival.heading: Inconsistency is not failure.
arrival.subheading: It is how most humans actually live. You are in good company.

arrival.heading: You are not starting over.
arrival.subheading: You are continuing with a gap in between. There is a difference.

arrival.heading: Some days work. Some don't.
arrival.subheading: Both count. You showed up today. Today counts.

arrival.heading: The rhythm is patient.
arrival.subheading: It waits for you. It is not bothered by the gap.

arrival.heading: Day by day.
arrival.subheading: Not streak by streak. Day by day is how this actually works.

arrival.heading: You did not lose it.
arrival.subheading: You paused. There is a difference between a pause and an ending.

release.heading: The guilt of starting over.
release.subheading: You don't have to earn your way back. You just come back.
release.field_placeholder: What are you judging yourself for right now...

release.heading: The gap.
release.subheading: How long were you away? It matters less than you think.
release.field_placeholder: How long since you last showed up for yourself...

release.heading: The worry about lost progress.
release.subheading: Rhythm is not about streaks. It is about the return.
release.field_placeholder: What do you feel you have lost or reset...

release.heading: The hard stretch behind you.
release.subheading: Set it down here. You do not have to carry it forward.
release.field_placeholder: What from the last few days needs to be released...

release.heading: The story you tell yourself.
release.subheading: About what kind of person keeps or breaks habits. What is it?
release.field_placeholder: What narrative are you running about your consistency...

release.heading: What made it hard.
release.subheading: Name the obstacle. It helps you understand the gap clearly.
release.field_placeholder: What got in the way of showing up recently...

release.heading: The expectation.
release.subheading: The one you had for yourself. Is it still a fair one?
release.field_placeholder: What were you expecting of yourself that felt out of reach...

breath.heading: One breath back.
breath.instruction: Slow inhale. Slow exhale. This is the return. Let it be this gentle.

breath.heading: No rush back.
breath.instruction: Breathe in for four counts. Out for six. The body does not judge the gap.

breath.heading: Present now.
breath.instruction: Breathe in. Feel both feet on the floor. You are here. That is what matters.

breath.heading: Steady.
breath.instruction: Three slow breaths. One for the past. One for today. One for beginning again.

breath.heading: The return breath.
breath.instruction: In through the nose. Out slowly. You came back. Let the breath acknowledge it.

completion.heading: You showed up.
completion.subheading: That was the whole task. And you did it.

completion.heading: One day back.
completion.subheading: Tomorrow, one more. Day by day is how this is built.

completion.heading: The return counts.
completion.subheading: Not the streak. Not the history. This return. Right here.

completion.heading: The rhythm holds.
completion.subheading: Even when you step away, it holds a place for you to return to.

completion.heading: You did not have to be perfect.
completion.subheading: You just had to show up. You did.

completion.heading: Small is not small.
completion.subheading: A return is not a small thing. It is the entire practice.

completion.heading: Day by day.
completion.subheading: That is how rhythm is built. You did today. That is enough.

actions.content: Do one thing from your usual routine, even if it's smaller than normal.
actions.why: Returning to routine, even partially, signals continuity to the mind.

actions.content: Set a time for tomorrow's check-in now.
actions.why: Scheduling the next return makes it easier to follow through.

actions.content: Write one sentence about how it feels to be back.
actions.why: Naming the feeling of return helps normalize it over time.

actions.content: Do five minutes of something you care about, then stop if needed.
actions.why: Five minutes is real. It is not nothing. The return counts.

actions.content: Drink a full glass of water before anything else.
actions.why: Small physical acts anchor the return in the body, not just the mind.

actions.content: Name one thing you want to do consistently this week.
actions.why: One thing is enough. More than that is too much to track right now.

actions.content: Do your usual ritual, even if it's shorter than normal.
actions.why: A shortened version still counts. The return matters, not the duration.

actions.content: Name three days this week you intend to show up.
actions.why: Intention written down becomes more likely to become action.

actions.content: Move your body for two minutes.
actions.why: Momentum starts in the body. Any movement counts as a return.

actions.content: Read one page of something you actually enjoy.
actions.why: A small pleasurable act reconnects you with the practice of showing up.

actions.content: Make your bed, or a simple version of it.
actions.why: Order in a small space creates a sense of forward motion.

actions.content: Write down the time you will begin tomorrow.
actions.why: A written start time increases follow-through significantly.

actions.content: Put your phone in another room for thirty minutes.
actions.why: Removing the main distraction makes the return easier to sustain.

actions.content: Sit somewhere comfortable and breathe for three minutes.
actions.why: The body needs to settle before a new rhythm can take hold.

actions.content: Reach out to one person you have not contacted in a while.
actions.why: Connection reactivates. Rhythms exist in relationships too.

actions.content: Do one task you have been avoiding for three days.
actions.why: Avoidance builds resistance. One action quietly breaks it.

actions.content: Write what went well last week, however small.
actions.why: Looking for the good shifts the story from failure to continuity.

actions.content: Set a consistent sleep time for this week.
actions.why: Sleep is where rhythm begins. Everything else follows from it.

actions.content: Spend five minutes outside.
actions.why: Natural light helps reset the body's internal timing.

actions.content: Clear one surface in your space.
actions.why: A cleaner environment makes returning to work feel easier.

actions.content: Write down what consistency means to you, personally.
actions.why: Your definition matters more than anyone else's version of it.

actions.content: Do one thing early in the day, before anything else.
actions.why: Early wins create forward motion for the rest of the day.

actions.content: Close open tabs or tasks you will not actually do today.
actions.why: Incomplete loops take attention. Closing them frees focus for the return.

actions.content: Tell one person you are back on track.
actions.why: Saying it out loud adds accountability and makes the return real.

actions.content: Notice one moment today that felt like you.
actions.why: Reconnecting with yourself is part of returning to rhythm.

actions.content: Write one sentence about what you want to build, long-term.
actions.why: Long-view thinking makes short-term inconsistency feel less catastrophic.

actions.content: Do something kind for your body today.
actions.why: The body is part of the rhythm. Treat it like it is.

actions.content: At the end of today, write one line: I showed up.
actions.why: The record of return matters. Over time, it becomes the evidence.

actions.content: Write one word that describes how today's return felt.
actions.why: A single word holds more than a paragraph sometimes. Find yours.

actions.content: Set your phone to do not disturb for the next ten minutes.
actions.why: Small protected windows make showing up feel more possible.
